If enabled, the secure application checks if the non-secure application has been programmed in non-secure flash before branching. If the non-secure application has not been programmed, then the secure application branches to an infinite loop in non-secure RAM. This prevents an issue where the debugger may not connect if the MCU is configured in the NSECSD lifecycle state.

The system clock (ICLK) is used as the operating clock of the CPU, DMAC, DTC, ROM, RAM, I/O ports and IIRFA. \nMaximum frequency is 240 MHz.
The Peripheral clock A (PCLKA) is used as the operating clock for the SCI, CANFD-RAM, CNECC, SPI, CRC, DOC, ADC12, DAC12, SCE5, GPT (bus clock), PDG and IIC. \nMaximum frequency is 120 MHz.
The Peripheral clock B (PCLKB) is used as the operating clock for all other modules not supported by PCLKA, PCLKC and PCLKD. \nMaximum frequency is 60 MHz.
The Peripheral clock C (PCLKC) is used as the operating clock for the ADC12 module. \nMaximum frequency is 60 MHz.
The Peripheral clock D (PCLKD) is used as the operating clock for the GPT (count clock) module. \nMaximum frequency is 120 MHz.

The flash-interface clock (FCLK) is used as the operating clock for the flash-memory interfaces.\nThat is, FCLK is used for programming and erasure of the ROM and E2 DataFlash, and reading from the E2 DataFlash. \nFrequency must be between 4 MHz and 60 MHz when any of these features are used.
Frequency output on the CLKOUT pin if CLKOUT is enabled. \nMaximum frequency is 24 MHz.
The SCISPI clock (SCISPICLK) is an operating clock for the SCISPI module. \nMaximum frequency is 120MHz.
The CANFD clock (CANFDCLK) is an operating clock for the CANFD module. \nMaximum frequency is 40 MHz.
The GPT clock (GPTCLK) is an operating clock for the GPT module. \nMaximum frequency is 200MHz.
The IIC clock (IICCLK) is an operating clock for the IIC module. \nMaximum frequency is 200MHz.
Clock frequency input to the GPT Module (GTCLK)\n Maximum frequency is 200 MHz.
